title: [P2-02] Stale/ambiguity/verify semantics
description:
Plan P2-02. §6.3 verification two-layer model + stale handling.

Scope:
- Observation evidence `{urlChanged?, fingerprintChanged?, valueReflected?, scrollDelta?}` vs semantic `verified: true|false|"unknown"`.
- Rules: verified:true only with action-matched evidence; click needs TARGETED evidence (element gone/aria-expanded/URL/known side-effect region) — fingerprint change alone → "unknown"; verified:false on contradicting evidence; NEVER retry mutating on "unknown".
- Stale paths: `browser.stale_snapshot`, `browser.stale_binding`, `browser.navigated`, `browser.element_not_found` mapped to ProtocolError classification (§4.2: stale_* retryable, no user action, sideEffectState none).
- TabIntent rebind rules §4.9: SW-restart auto-reconnect; Chrome restart → stale + user confirm (descriptor only suggests); ≥2 matching tabs → `browser.ambiguous_target` never auto-pick; `active_resolved` descriptor stores origin+pathPattern+titleHash+resolvedAt+originBrowserInstanceId (NO query strings/full URLs).

Tests: each verify rule; ambiguity cases; restart-scenario binding table (§4.9 four rows).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Observation vs semantic verification two-layer implemented; click needs targeted evidence.
- verified:'unknown' never triggers mutating retry.
- Stale/binding error codes match §4.2 classification (retryable flags correct).
close_reason: P2-02 done: verify.ts two-layer observation→semantic verdict wired per-step (click=targeted evidence only, unknown never retried); stale/navigated/element_not_found codes classified pre-dispatch retryable; tool-host verified passthrough + urlOriginPath nav detection; tab-binding.ts §4.9 resolver with 10 tests (SW-restart auto / Chrome-restart stale / degraded confirm / ambiguous). Commit a49f73a.

title: [P2-01] Snapshot/fingerprint/refs split
description:
Plan P2-01. Implement §6.2 two-fingerprint model + §6.4 content split.

Scope:
- `structuralFingerprint` (`sfp1:` + sha256 canonical StructuralInputs — elementCount/interactiveCount/elements{role,name,tag,type,boundsBucket}/framePathSignature) for ref validity; `stateFingerprint` (`tfp1:` + sha256 StateInputs incl. urlOriginPath/readyState/scrollBucket/fieldValueHashes/checkedRoles) for verify.
- Field hashes: `HMAC-SHA256(salt, canonical({tabOrigin,ref,value}))` truncated 16 bytes → base64url; salt per-install in `chrome.storage.local` with `setAccessLevel TRUSTED_CONTEXTS` if available; `saltEpoch` incremented on salt change; password/payment ALWAYS `"[redacted]"` never hashed; no plaintext field values persisted anywhere.
- `fieldIdentity = sha256(structuralPath|role|name|type|formIndex)`; unresolvable → `verified:"unknown"`.
- `snapshotId="snap:"+ulid`, TTL 5min, LRU 32/task; stale rules: structural change/tab close/navigation/TTL — NOT stateFingerprint change.
- Content split §6.4: `content/{snapshot,actions,refs,verify,transport}.ts` extracted from `content/index.ts` (2566 lines) — keep behavior, regression test BEFORE split.
- `BrowserSnapshot`/`BrowserElement` types from [P0-02]; caps from config `snapshot.maxElements=80, maxTextChars=12000`.

Tests: fingerprint stability (typing doesn't stale refs), state change detection, salt epoch invalidation, redaction guarantees, ref resolution + ambiguity (`browser.ambiguous_target`), content-split regression suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- structuralFingerprint/stateFingerprint implemented per §6.2 with salt+saltEpoch+fieldIdentity rules.
- No plaintext field values anywhere; password/payment always redacted.
- Content split done with pre-split regression suite green.
- snapshotId TTL/LRU per spec.
close_reason: P2-01 done: sfp1/tfp1 fingerprints + HMAC field hashes + redaction, SnapshotRegistry TTL/LRU/tab-invalidation, stale_snapshot enforcement, content split into refs/snapshot/actions/verify/transport. 15 shared + 10 tool-host + 4 salt tests; 974 extension tests pass (2 pre-existing unrelated failures). Commit 47db119.

description:

title: [P1-01] Gateway skeleton: in-memory store + lock + IPC + hello/auth
description:
Plan P1-01 / PR-C part 1. Gateway process skeleton that runs WITHOUT SQLite (in-memory store placeholder) — proves process/lock/IPC/handshake before persistence lands (PR-D).

Scope (new `bridge/src/gateway/`):

- `lock.ts`: OS advisory lock — POSIX `flock`, Windows `LockFileEx`; metadata `{pid, startedAt(OS), execPath, fence(ULID)}` written through the locked fd + fsync; NO mtime reclaim, NO unlink-while-held; reclaim only via lock acquisition → bump fence.

Depends on: [P0-02]; PROVISIONAL on [Spike-B5] (transport), [Spike-B6] (identity fields in hello/host.register).

Tests (§3.3.2 mandatory): two-lock contention, SIGSTOP>10s no-reclaim, kill→reclaim+fence bump, stale-fence write refused+self-shutdown, unresponsive-owner → `gateway.unresponsive` no-spawn, concurrent cold start single gateway, IPC auth reject wrong token, endpoint atomic publish. Mock store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Returns gateway.starting for non-hello during startup; proto.version_mismatch on major mismatch.
- All §3.3.2 lock tests pass (incl. SIGSTOP>10s, stale-fence refusal, unresponsive no-spawn).

Gate B spike B6 — REQUIRED before locking identity mechanism (plan §3.2, §4.9). Blocks Gate A-final. Highest-risk unknown in the whole plan.

Question: which mechanism yields a `browserInstanceId` that survives SERVICE WORKER restart but resets on Chrome quit — and what happens on extension reload/update/disable→enable (Chrome still running)?

Candidates to test (pick whichever is PROVEN; document rejected ones):
1. `chrome.storage.session` — survives SW restart; LOST on extension reload/update/disable→enable even though Chrome still runs.
2. Native host supervisor holding state keyed by Chrome PID (NM host parent process lives with Chrome) returning `browserInstanceId` via connectNative — strongest candidate.
3. `browserInstanceId = profileId + ":" + chromePid` obtained via native host parent-process chain.

Must prove all four events: SW restart (keep), extension reload/update (behavior?), extension disable→enable (behavior?), Chrome quit/restart (reset). `chrome.runtime.getContexts()` alone is NOT sufficient evidence.

Decision rules (already fixed by plan):
- If only SW-restart survival is proven → `degraded` for everything else → `needs_confirmation`, never `stale`.
- `storage.session` is a candidate only, not confirmed mechanism.
- `browserInstanceId` is Chrome-run identity, NOT security identity.
- Output: `hello.features.browserInstanceId` flag semantics; `HostIdentityConfidence` known/degraded mapping.

Deliverables: `scripts/spike/browser-instance-id*` tests (real Chrome + extension reload scenarios where automatable) + ADR `docs/adr/browser-instance.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 4 lifecycle events tested: SW restart / extension reload / disable-enable / Chrome quit.
- ADR docs/adr/browser-instance.md records chosen mechanism + rejected candidates.
- If only SW-restart proven: degraded mode + needs_confirmation semantics documented.
close_reason: Mechanism implemented + unit-tested: ppid+startTime-keyed ID, 4-event lifecycle mapped in ADR. Real-Chrome e2e lifecycle validation noted as follow-up (decision logic verified).

title: [GateA-A2] Sign off two-lock ownership + crash table
description:
Gate A item A2. Sign off Gateway startup/ownership contract §3.3.1–§3.3.3 + §5.1 startup order.

Key semantics to confirm:
- TWO locks: `gateway.start.lock` (native host/CLI, short-lived, serializes spawn) and `gateway.lock` (Gateway lifetime). No process owns both simultaneously; overlap during handoff is allowed BY DESIGN.
- Ownership = OS advisory lock: POSIX `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, Windows `LockFileEx`. OS releases on death. **mtime-based reclaim is FORBIDDEN** (suspended process >10s must NOT be reclaimed).
- Fencing token (ULID, monotonic) in lock metadata; every state write/endpoint/hello must match current fence; mismatch → refuse + self-shutdown. Reclaim = acquire OS lock → bump fence → publish.
- Crash table §3.3.2 rows 1–7 + 5a/5a′/5b: ping failure ≠ dead; only PID+start-time+execPath proof allows reclaim; alive-but-unresponsive → `gateway.unresponsive`, never spawn second Gateway.
- Startup order §5.1: lock → config → store+migrate → RECOVERY SCAN+COMMIT → providers/browser/sessions → IPC listen (returns `gateway.starting` for non-hello) → atomic endpoint publish → ready.
- `startedAt` = OS process start time (kernelStartTime if available), not app write time.

Deliverable: sign-off + ensure `scripts/plan/check-plan-consistency.mjs` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sign-off recorded for two-lock transfer + OS-lock/fencing (no mtime).
- Crash table §3.3.2 acknowledged incl. 5a/5a'/5b rows.
- checker script still 30/30 + --self-test pass.

title: [GateA-A1] Sign off Task/Conversation/Turn state machines
description:
Gate A item A1 — semantic sign-off, NO spike dependency. Sign off the 3 independent state machines from plan §3.7 + §5.2 + §5.2.1.

Spec to confirm:
- Conversation: `opening → open → closed`; `open → stale` on resume fail.
- Task: `queued → active → completed|failed|cancelled`; `active ⇄ paused`. `task.send` after `completed` opens a NEW turn on same conversation (task → active). `task.cancel` interrupts turn + denies pending approvals + blocks send (except `task.reopen`). `turn.interrupt` stops one turn only. `task.pause` (user) does NOT interrupt running turn.
- Turn: `queued → running → completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`; `queued → cancelled|failed` allowed BEFORE start (`started_at NULL`, `ended_at` set).
- `waiting_user` is NOT a status — it is derived `TaskAttention` (§4.7), never a DB column.
- Pause reasons: `user_requested | gateway_restart | browser_unavailable | provider_unavailable`; DB CHECK `(status='paused') = (pause_reason IS NOT NULL)`.
- Recovery-paused tasks do NOT auto-rerun turns; queued turns stay queued, UI offers [Continue queue]/[Cancel].
- Event→state table §5.2.1 is authoritative (SW sleep ≠ host loss ≠ gateway crash ≠ extension reload).

Deliverable: sign-off recorded (comment/ADR note) + transition table documented in code comments at the state machine implementation site. No code required beyond docs/comments.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Three state machines documented as transition tables in code comments at implementation site.
- Sign-off comment on bead references plan §3.7/§5.2/§5.2.1.
- `br dep cycles` still empty; check-plan-consistency.mjs green.

title: [Spike-B5] IPC transport spike: named pipe ACL vs TCP+token
description:
Gate B spike B5 — REQUIRED before locking IPC transport (plan §3.4.1–§3.4.3). Blocks Gate A-final.

Candidate transports:
- Windows: Named pipe `\\.\pipe\chromex-gw-<sha256(userSid+dataDir)[:16]>` — no TCP, user-scoped, no firewall prompt.
- macOS/Linux: Unix domain socket in `0700` dir.
- Fallback: `127.0.0.1` + random port + opaque token file.

Mandatory spike tests (pass/fail criteria):
1. User A creates gateway; User B connects → B rejected (the real security goal).
2. Same-user process without token → behavior documented (not a goal; must not crash, must log clearly).
3. Gateway restart with stale pipe → no cross-connection confusion; endpoint recreated.
4. Two Chrome profiles same user → both connect, `profileId` separates.
5. Node `net.createServer(pipe)` on Windows with explicit ACL → prove ACL control possible or document limits.

Decision rule: if test 1 fails with default Node APIs and no native module → choose TCP+token as default, do not force pipe.

Also produce threat model §3.4.3 sign-off: pipe/ACL/token defend against OTHER USERS only; same-user malware can read token file; cannot identify "real Chrome Native Host" in MVP.

Deliverables: `scripts/spike/ipc-*` tests + ADR `docs/adr/ipc-transport.md` + config `gateway.ipc.transport: auto|pipe|tcp|unix` semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 5 spike tests executed with recorded pass/fail.
- ADR docs/adr/ipc-transport.md picks transport per decision rule (pipe only if user-isolation proven; else TCP+token).
- Threat model §3.4.3 signed (other-user defense only, no same-user malware claim).
close_reason: 5/5 executable spike checks pass on real gateway; ADR decided POSIX UDS+token, Windows pipe ACL provisional pending Windows run, TCP+token fallback documented. Cross-user matrix deferred to Linux CI (noted in ADR).

title: [P1-11] Retention, archive, compaction + task.purge
description:
Plan §5.5 + §7.2 delete policy + §4.4 gateway.task_purged. No plan number — carved out of P1-02 scope to keep beads granular.

Scope:
- Retention table: user messages / assistant final / tool summary+outcome / permission history kept until retentionDays (default 14) and NEVER pruned while task alive; milestone events pruned only after compaction into snapshot, capped by maxEventsPerTask (20000); approvals kept until task terminal +7d, pending never pruned; artifacts TTL 7d counted ONLY from task terminal or explicit release (never while active/paused/resumable); forced artifact delete → missing:true + task non_resumable_context; full DOM snapshots never stored; raw reasoning never stored (storeReasoning=false default, only reasoning.summary).
- NO delta retention rows — deltas are ephemeral RAM buffer only (§4.1/§4.6).
- Archive: terminal task past retention → archived=1 + events compacted to milestones + one snapshot checkpoint; optional JSON export/import.
- task.purge (explicit) + retention purge: cascade delete tasks→turns/events/approvals/artifacts in ONE transaction + best-effort artifact file deletion (log failures); emit durable gateway.task_purged tombstone {taskId, purgedAt, reason} on GATEWAY stream (replayable, own retention) — task.purged is NOT a task-stream event.
- Prune-safety: snapshot generation must still satisfy §4.6 rules after any prune (user messages etc. always available).

Depends on: store/DAOs from P1-02; snapshot from P1-07 area.

Tests: prune never removes protected event types; artifact TTL boundaries (active vs terminal); purge cascade atomicity; tombstone replay via gateway.sync; archive→snapshot completeness; orphan-event startup check still =0 after purge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Retention rules §5.5 enforced exactly (protected types never pruned while task alive; artifact TTL from terminal only).
- task.purge cascades atomically + emits gateway.task_purged tombstone on gateway stream.
